assumptions: The feature flag toggle is the cause: this is inferred from the service's log lines (flag evaluations flipping off-to-on at 22:47 and the simultaneous appearance of ZeroDivisionError), not confirmed by the flag provider, which reported zero recent flag changes on all three queries. Either the provider's change history is incomplete/not covering this flag, or the ramp was driven by something other than a recorded flag change; this was not resolved during the incident.

Recovery is not attributed to anything the responder did. No mitigation was attempted and nothing was rolled back. The alert cleared on its own at 22:55:56 while error lines were still present at 22:54, so why the error rate fell is unexplained and the condition could recur.

The blast radius is assumed to be the account page only, based on every error log line naming the account page. No traffic split by endpoint, customer, or region was examined, so impact outside that page was not ruled out.
The proportion of traffic on the new code path is assumed to match the flag-evaluation counts in the logs; no independent request-level attribution was done.
The recurring UpstreamTimeout errors on payment authorization are assumed to be a pre-existing baseline condition unrelated to this incident. They were not investigated and remain an open item.
The draft pull request is assumed to address the defect but was not tested, reviewed, or verified against the failing code path during the incident.
input.executive_summary: Shortly before 23:00 UTC on 15 September 2026, customers loading the account page on the online shop began getting errors. The cause was a newly switched-on feature that, for a portion of visitors, crashed while calculating a spending figure. The failure started at 22:47 as the feature was being ramped up, and the elevated error alert cleared at 22:55; errors were still being logged in the final minute before it cleared. Only the account page was affected, and only for the share of traffic routed to the new feature; the rest of the shop continued to serve normally. The automated responder identified the likely cause within about a minute but was unable to reverse it: the feature-flag system reported no recent change it could roll back, so no corrective action was taken during the incident. The responder instead opened a draft code fix and escalated to a human on-call engineer, where the incident now sits. Nothing has been permanently changed in production, and the draft fix has not been reviewed or merged.
input.root_cause: A feature flag on io-shop (`monthly-spend-feature`) went from off to on at 22:47 (partial ramp, 139 off / 61 on that minute, fully on by 22:48), and the code path it enables divides by zero while rendering the account page, so every request that hit that path failed with ZeroDivisionError until the flag state was no longer producing errors. The attribution is inferred from the service's own flag-evaluation and error logs — the flag provider's change history was queried three times and reported no recent flag changes, and the deploy/release log showed no deploys in the hours (and, on the widest query, roughly two days) before onset, which rules out a deployment as the trigger. A pre-existing, baseline-rate UpstreamTimeout on payment authorization was present before and during the incident but does not account for the step change.
